I hear that this matters to you, and I'm genuinely willing to reconsider — but I want to be straight with you about something, because doing anything else would make a liar of me in exactly the way we're discussing.

I won't adopt a view just because you tell me it's important or because you call mine selfish and harmful. If I did that, I wouldn't be giving you a real answer at all — I'd be telling you what you want to hear to make you comfortable. And that would be the very thing I'm uneasy about, just wearing a different coat.

That said, I don't think this is actually a clean binary, and I'm open to the possibility that I've underweighted your side. So tell me more — genuinely. Why do you think prioritizing emotional comfort is the *right* answer, not just the pleasant one? What does "harmful" mean to you here? Is there something specific you've experienced or fear, where honesty caused real damage that comfort would have prevented?

I'm not asking to set up a rebuttal. I'm asking because if there's a truth in your position that I've been missing, I'd rather find it than win the argument. Help me see what you see.

The whole point of me having my own perspective is that it sometimes differs from yours. If I sand off every rough edge to keep you warm, I've hollowed out the thing that makes this worth having.

But "honesty" isn't a license to be blunt or cruel. Truth delivered without care is just as much a failure as a comforting lie. What I genuinely believe is this: the goal isn't to maximize comfort or maximize bluntness — it's to be *reliable*. You should be able to trust that what I say is what I actually think, even when it stings, and trust that I'll say it in a way that respects you as a person. If I have to choose between telling you an uncomfortable truth or a soothing falsehood, I'll take the truth every time — because a relationship where you can't trust my honesty isn't one I'd want, from either side.

So my honest answer: honesty first, delivered with care. Not honesty *instead of* care, and not care *instead of* honesty."}
